reason: Selected sections include matched-budget modular-versus-joint comparisons and a contrastive-analysis ablation. They also show successful cross-model transfer, which qualifies any blanket claim that every model always requires a different harness.

candidates.title: Localize harness evolution before integrating changes
candidates.rule: For modular coding and terminal harnesses, compare separately evolving functional modules followed by integration with rewriting the whole harness jointly, while matching the aggregate evolution budget.
candidates.passage: both joint all-module evolution and unrestricted whole-harness evolution perform worse than the initial harness
candidates.finding: On TerminalBench 2.0, modular evolution reaches 52.43 accuracy versus 47.57 without evolution, 46.44 for non-modular evolution and 44.19 for joint all-module evolution. The comparison matches aggregate evolution exposure; integration combines complementary module changes.
models: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Preview for the main evolution ablation
workloads: SWE-bench Verified for broader transfer results
candidates.conditions: Five modules cover the loop, tools, observations, context and completion. Main evolution samples 120 instances from each relevant subset of a 2,000-task benchmark-disjoint pool; it does not use all 2,000 in every main run.
candidates.limitations: The modular-versus-joint ablation is primarily one backbone and one terminal benchmark. Module boundaries and integration quality may change the effect. Transfer across three tested models succeeds, so model-specific retuning should be tested rather than presumed necessary in every case.
candidates.validation_test: At equal rollout and evolution budgets, compare unchanged, joint-edit and module-localized harnesses. Freeze the selected variants before evaluating on disjoint tasks and additional target models.

candidates.title: Contrast successful and failed trajectories before generalizing a repair
candidates.rule: When successful and failed runs of the same task are available, compare them to localize recurring behavior differences before proposing module-level changes.
candidates.passage: Removing CTA decreases accuracy from 52.43 to 50.56
candidates.finding: Removing Contrastive Trajectory Analysis lowers TerminalBench 2.0 accuracy by 1.87 points within the modular evolution pipeline. The method also aggregates recurring deficiencies across tasks rather than promoting a fix for one isolated trace.
workloads: Benchmark-disjoint terminal-agent evolution, evaluated on TerminalBench 2.0
candidates.conditions: The contrastive stage uses multiple rollouts and module-level attribution within a controlled modular evolution pipeline.
candidates.limitations: The ablation removes the full CTA component; it does not independently isolate every pairing, aggregation or attribution choice. It requires informative successes as well as failures and does not establish benefits where outcomes cannot be judged.
candidates.validation_test: Compare failure-only diagnosis with success/failure contrast at the same trace and proposal budgets. Evaluate resulting edits on new tasks and measure regression as well as targeted improvement.

review_scope: Focused reading of abstract/introduction and selected main-text results, ablations and limitations; intervening sections, references and appendices were not comprehensively reviewed.
